| [THEORY-023](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-023.md) v4 | Evidence cannot settle AI consciousness | Birch (2025), [LIT-111](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-111.md): behavioural markers are "gamed", and architectural markers are "Janus-faced", giving a two-level deadlock. | [THEORY-031](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-031.md) v2 | Detection criteria differ only in threshold | Peterson & Birdsall (1953), [LIT-364](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-364.md) — the threshold on ℓ = f_SN/f_N is optimal for expected value and at fixed false-alarm rate, and the two optimum families coincide (Part I Thms 1–7). The ROC's slope equals the threshold (Thm 8). Tanner & Swets (1954), [LIT-368](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-368.md), carry this over to the human observer as d′ plus a criterion. Stanislaw & Todorov (1999), [LIT-367](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-367.md), state that d′ varies with the criterion unless the variances are equal. | [THEORY-043](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-043.md) v6 | Nested-agent minds split on unprincipled criteria | Minsky's society of mind builds a mind downward, out of agents that are not minds. Schwitzgebel ([LIT-159](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-159.md)) builds a candidate mind upward, out of agents that are. The readings agree that agency survives both directions: Block grants a homunculi-head beliefs, List grants organised groups agency and awareness, Levin finds nested goal-pursuing collectives (his "Selves") at every scale. The dispute narrows to phenomenal consciousness, and every published way to accept the downward move while refusing the upward one is either an anti-nesting principle (Putnam's stipulation, IIT's exclusion postulate, Kammerer's functional version), each introduced for or justified weakly by the verdict it gives, or an architectural criterion that would count against a loosely coupled society of mind as much as against a nation. Proposed: an account of where a dispute stands, from philosophical argument and no measurement. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-044](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-044.md) v2 | Self as context is a learned deictic perspective | Barnes-Holmes et al. ([LIT-541](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-541.md)) define three selves: the conceptualized self, the content of verbal relations about oneself; the knowing self, their ongoing process; and the transcendent self, their context. Hayes et al. ([LIT-555](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-555.md)) say the third arises from deictic frames (I–you, here–there, now–then) as "a sense of self as a locus or perspective", and is "a context for verbal knowing, not the content", so its limits "cannot be consciously known". The account maps the three onto the record's holdings: the content is the narrative self (Dennett, Gallagher, Strawson), and the context is what Hume could not find among his perceptions and what Metzinger calls a transparent perspective. It differs from the minimal self (Gallagher) on origin: RFT says the perspective is learned in language. The evidence for the learned origin is cited, not read, so Proposed. The clinical claim is [THEORY-051](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-051.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-048](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-048.md) | Biology implements psychological functions | Kendler (2008), [LIT-539](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-539.md): following Marr, a lower-level theory either replaces a higher-level construct (temperature by mean kinetic energy) or implements it, and in psychiatry biology "will implement but not replace psychology". The thesis is argued from neuroscience's successes in perception, learning and memory, not from a psychiatric case, so it is Proposed. It is a thesis about explanation, not about distinct mental causes: it survives Pernu's argument ([LIT-147](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-147.md)) that the neural evidence supports only mental causation by identity. Kendler 2005 ([LIT-552](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-552.md)), which argued the mind–brain propositions this paper develops, is unread. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-050](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-050.md) | Psychological inflexibility is transdiagnostic | Hayes et al. ([LIT-541](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-541.md)) give the mechanism: once a word stands in derived relation to an event it can carry that event's aversive functions, so private events become worth avoiding. | [THEORY-055](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-055.md) | Appraisal elicits emotion as action readiness | Frijda, Ridderinkhof & Rietveld (2014), [LIT-540](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-540.md), Frijda's own late statement of the theory of The Emotions ([LIT-546](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-546.md), unread). An automatic appraisal of how an event bears on one's concerns elicits a state of action readiness: a motive to change one's relation to the object, with control precedence. Emotions differ by mode (hostility for anger, avoidance for fear), and "in the absence of concern pertinence … no emotion". It is the record's only read statement of an appraisal theory, because Lazarus ([LIT-550](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-550.md)) is unread. Both the elicitation claim and the claim that emotions differ by mode are argued, and neither is tested. The second is partly definitional within the theory. Rivals [THEORY-057](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-057.md): both accounts let instances vary and group them by function, but the appraisal account puts the unity in the agent's readiness and the constructionist account puts it in the perceiver's concept. Proposed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-056](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-056.md) v5 | Regulation is not separate from emotion generation | Frijda, Ridderinkhof & Rietveld (2014), [LIT-540](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-540.md), deny "the exclusivity of emotion regulation processes". Barrett (2017), [LIT-542](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-542.md), reaches the second half from the opposite side of the emotion debate: automaticity and control are "different brain modes … not two battling brain systems", and she offers as a hypothesis that reappraisal works by the same predictions that construct emotion. | [THEORY-057](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-057.md) | Emotion categories are not natural kinds | Barrett (2017), [LIT-542](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-542.md): degeneracy, population thinking, and a table of findings in which no region, network, pattern or neuron is consistent for an emotion category. From these she concludes that categories such as fear are populations of variable instances, grouped by a goal and constructed by categorization with a concept. She rejects basic-emotion and causal appraisal theories as positing a "Lockean essence". This is the record's only read statement of the view. The record's philosophy holdings sharpen it. Pernu ([LIT-147](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-147.md)) shows that many-to-one realisation at a fine grain does not rule out one variable at a coarser grain, so degeneracy alone does not carry the conclusion, and Table 1 has to. Searle ([LIT-482](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-482.md)) shows that Barrett's comparison with money is to observer-relative function, not to institutions. Rivals the appraisal account, [THEORY-055](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-055.md). Proposed: one theoretical paper, no independent test, and the reply unread. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-061](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-061.md) | Goals set accumulation parameters, not responses | Bogacz et al. | [THEORY-063](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-063.md) v2 | Unity of experience needs no self-model | Metzinger's précis of Being No One (2005), [LIT-568](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-568.md): the globality constraint makes every conscious content part of one world-model. | [THEORY-064](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-064.md) | Self is an unrecognised self-model's content | Metzinger's précis of Being No One (2005), [LIT-568](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-568.md), with his encyclopedia article "Self models" ([LIT-450](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-450.md)): a phenomenal self is a transparent self-model, one whose representational character "is not accessible to subjective experience", so that the system experiences its content "simply as ourselves". | [THEORY-068](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-068.md) v2 | Leaky accumulators optimal only when balanced | Bogacz et al. ([LIT-569](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-569.md)) prove that the pure drift diffusion model is the continuum limit of the sequential probability ratio test, and so the optimal two-choice decider, and that the linearised Usher–McClelland network reduces to it exactly when leak equals inhibition (and, for free response, when both are also large). Usher and McClelland ([LIT-565](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-565.md)) derived the difference of the two units as an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process with net leak K = k − β: K ≠ 0 caps accuracy, leak-dominant weights late evidence and inhibition-dominant early. Active because the core is derivation, checkable on paper. | [THEORY-070](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-070.md) | Control allocation is a cost-benefit computation | Shenhav, Botvinick & Cohen ([LIT-585](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-585.md)) unify dACC's many reported functions as one: deciding whether, where and how much control to allocate. The paper reviews evidence and fits nothing, so Proposed. It does not say what the cost is, how EVC is computed, or that it governs emotion regulation. | Proposed |

| [THEORY-089](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-089.md) | Content has narrow-role and referential factors | Block (1986), [LIT-648](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-648.md), and Block (1987), [LIT-625](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-625.md). Meaning has a conceptual-role component "entirely 'in the head'", an expression's "total causal role, abstractly described" in inference and decision, which twins share and which explains their behaviour, and an external component relating representations to referents and truth conditions. Conceptual role fixes the nature of the referential factor, not reference. A one-factor theory with long-arm roles must, to get Twin Earth truth conditions right, import normal context, causal chains of borrowed reference and experts; chop off what lies outside the skin and the rest is the short-arm role, so the difference is "merely verbal". Social meaning is assigned to the referential factor or to a third, social factor, and is only sketched. Proposed: no identity conditions for roles, and narrow content is given room, not shown explanatory. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-091](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-091.md) | Joint loss doesn't show a phenomenal function | Block (1995), [LIT-643](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-643.md), §6. Marcel, Flanagan, van Gulick and Schacter argue from the thirsty blindsight patient who does not reach for the water, and Searle from Penfield's petit mal automatisms, that a function of phenomenal consciousness is to let information guide action. In blindsight access is missing too, and in petit mal nothing shows experience is missing at all. "The fallacy is: an obvious function of the machinery of access-consciousness is illicitly transferred to phenomenal consciousness." That experience causes access, so that the function is experience's after all, is "a bold hypothesis, not a fallacy", and the deficit cannot decide it. Proposed: single-source, and the distinction it rests on is argued from conceivable cases. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-092](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-092.md) v3 | Behavioural capacity doesn't fix intelligence | Block (1981), [LIT-642](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-642.md): the strongest behaviourist conception of intelligence, a capacity to give sensible responses to any sequence of inputs, "whatever they may be", is met by a machine that stores every sensible conversation of a test's length and looks up its next reply, yet "the machine has the intelligence of a toaster". So psychologism is true: two systems alike in all actual and counterfactual behaviour can differ in intelligence through the processing that mediates it. Block (1995), [LIT-630](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-630.md), n. 1: the same machine refutes the wider claim that there is no mental difference without a behavioural one. It is a claim about constitution, not evidence: performance stays evidence for competence. It names no required kind of processing, and its machine is a lookup table, not a trained network. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-094](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-094.md) | Neither report nor no-report isolates the NCC | Block (2007), [LIT-646](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-646.md), framed the methodological puzzle: the neural basis of experience can be found only by deciding whether it includes the machinery of access, and the evidence comes through report. The no-report paradigm was the answer. Block (2019), [LIT-637](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-637.md), argues it has "a fatal flaw": subjects not asked to report still think about what they see, and that thought is aligned with the percept (the "bored monkey" problem). Eliminating report isolates the basis of experience "only if it eliminates post-perceptual cognitive processing" correlated with the percept. Brascamp et al.'s inconspicuous rivalry, whose switches subjects detected at chance, is the one such design Block offers. The method is specific to rivalry so far, and Block says there may be no general solution. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-095](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-095.md) v3 | Inverted Earth leaves only internal accounts | Block (1990), [LIT-634](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-634.md): on Inverted Earth colours and colour words are inverted, so a subject fitted with inverting lenses notices nothing. After long residence, or for a twin with a molecule-for-molecule identical brain raised there, the intentional content of the experience of the sky inverts and so does its long-arm functional role, while qualitative content stays the same; Q = F₁, Q = F₂ and F₁ ≠ F₂ breaks transitivity of identity. Block (2003), [LIT-635](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-635.md), turns the case on externalist representationism: for colour there is no shared appearance property left to explain the sameness, and long-term memory blocks the gradual-shift reply, so "mental paint" is what stays the same. Proposed: both rest on an externalist shift of content and on first-person sameness, and Block concedes that a short-arm functional theory of qualia would escape. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-096](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-096.md) | Consciousness is global neuronal ignition | Mashour, Roelfsema, Changeux & Dehaene (2020), [LIT-631](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-631.md), a review by the theory's proponents. Conscious access is "a non-linear network ignition" that amplifies and sustains a representation so that local processors can access it, in a distributed core of long-range layer II/III and V pyramidal neurons with prefrontal cortex a key hub but "not ... the exclusive territory". Ignition is exclusive: one content at a time. Evidence: seen and unseen trials diverge after about 200 ms across modalities; in van Vugt et al.'s monkeys, missed stimuli drove V1 and V4 but only reported ones, and false alarms, ignited sustained prefrontal firing, and the signal-detection threshold is the ignition threshold. The review adopts the premise that global availability "is what we subjectively experience as a conscious state", and calls experience without access untested; that premise, not the access data, is where it rivals overflow and the sensory account. Single source, second-hand evidence, and the P3 question conceded open. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-097](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-097.md) | Distant co-ripples carry forebrain coordination | Verzhbinsky, Daume, Cheng, Rutishauser & Halgren (2026), [LIT-633](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-633.md): in 1,373 single units from five bilateral forebrain regions of 35 epilepsy patients doing a Sternberg task, ripples (70–100 Hz, about 70 ms) co-occur between bundles at a median 5% at every tract distance from 71 to 223 mm, and unit pairs co-fire a median 34% more during co-ripples than in no-ripple periods, beyond a rate-only null and with no loss over distance. The gain rises with load (13% in maintenance, 19% at retrieval), and encoding co-firing for a stimulus recurs at retrieval in 0.29% of cell-pair trials in co-ripples against 0.14% outside them. Correlational throughout: one task, two load levels, clinically placed electrodes, nothing perturbed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-098](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-098.md) v4 | Consciousness is sensory recurrence, not PFC | Block's "back of the head" position, from three papers. Block (2005), [LIT-629](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-629.md): a phenomenal NCC (for seen motion, recurrent MT/V5–V1 activity) and an access NCC (frontoparietal broadcasting), with winner-take-all access letting a recurrent sensory representation lose and stay unaccessed. Proposed: an inference to the best explanation, with every experiment second-hand and the decisive test not yet run. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-100](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-100.md) | Conscious report correlate needs no laminar cortex | Maldarelli & Güntürkün (2025), [LIT-650](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-650.md), reviewing Nieder et al. (2020): in crows reporting near-threshold stimuli, single neurons in the nidopallium caudolaterale (NCL), the functional analogue of prefrontal cortex, fired with the "seen" report whether or not a stimulus was shown and were silent on "not seen" reports. NCL is nuclear, not layered; the cortex-like layers and columns found in birds are confined to the sensory pallium. So a correlate of conscious report does not need laminar cortex. The crow evidence is second-hand, from one laboratory and not in the record, and a report paradigm cannot separate access from phenomenal consciousness. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-102](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-102.md) v3 | Ventral code is sustained; prefrontal is transient | Vishne, Gerber, Knight & Deouell (2023), [LIT-644](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-644.md): in 430 visually responsive subdural electrodes from 10 patients viewing images for 300–1,500 ms with no report on analysed trials, high-frequency activity and single-electrode category selectivity fell about 80% from peak by 800–900 ms, while the pattern across ventral temporal electrodes kept near-ceiling, time-invariant category and exemplar information that ended a fixed delay after the image went off. Prefrontal and parietal information was confined to about 150–600 ms and ignored duration. This met the predictions both IIT's and the global workspace's proponents registered for the paradigm, so it did not discriminate them. | [THEORY-103](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-103.md) v3 | Phenomenal experience overflows access | Block (2007), [LIT-646](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-646.md), and Block (2011), [LIT-640](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-640.md). Subjects shown 8–32 items say they see all or almost all of them, report about 4, and when cued after offset can report or compare most of any cued subset: capacity 6–7 of 8 up to 1.5 s (Landman et al.), and 7, 6 and 5 of 8 at 1, 2.5 and 4 s (fragile visual short-term memory), against a working memory that stays at about 4. Block reads the surplus as experienced. The rival "sparse" reading holds it in an unconscious store plus a conscious generic or fragmentary image, and Block argues there is no independent evidence for either posit. Proposed: every experiment is second-hand, and that the surplus is conscious is the contested step. Overflow means most items are unaccessed, not that any is inaccessible. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-124](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-124.md) v2 | Selectivity clusters in only 3 of ~20 areas | Posani et al. (2026), [LIT-708](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-708.md): in about 14,000 cortical units of the IBL Brainwide Map, the 8-variable selectivity profiles of 4,617 selective neurons beat a covariance-matched Gaussian null for clustering within a region only in VISp, AUDp and SSp-ul. | [THEORY-125](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-125.md) | Group emotion is possible, though none is shown | Huebner (2010), [LIT-702](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-702.md): a genuinely collective emotion is a state of a group that "could not be exhaustively characterized in terms of intentional states of individuals in aggregation". Fear requires danger detection, redeployment of attention, system-wide preparatory change and their coordination into one state with indicative content and imperative force; a distributed system can integrate routines that way. Some individual emotions are non-conscious, so a group's need not be felt, and emotion kinds are functional ("like vodka"), so lacking homologous mechanisms does not exclude groups. The paper establishes a possibility, not an instance: its worked case, the USS Palau crew, turns out to be "collective detection of danger in the absence of a fear response", and the replacement, the 2008 McCain–Palin campaign, is offered as "intuitively plausible" pending anthropological data. Proposed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-137](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-137.md) v3 | Mind attributions shape the institutions | Tollefsen (2025), [LIT-736](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-736.md). Both sides of the group-mind debate treat ascription as tracking pre-existing causes. On the regulative view of folk psychology it shapes its target. In United States v. Bank of New England a court held a bank to know what no employee knew, and banks then built systems to detect reportable deposits. Narratives regulate too. Proposed: the regulative view is assumed, and the effect on banks is asserted, not documented. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-155](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-155.md) v3 | Bayesian iterated learning converges to the prior | Griffiths & Kalish (2007), [LIT-769](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-769.md), read in [NOTE-599](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-599.md): a chain of learners who share a prior and each sample a hypothesis from their posterior is a Gibbs sampler, so the probability a learner holds a hypothesis converges to its prior probability, whatever the amount of data passed on; with MAP learners the outcome centres on the prior's mode but depends on data amount and noise, and can amplify weak biases. It is a theorem about an idealized chain. It does not say human chains reach the prior, and Kirby, Cornish & Smith's laboratory chains, [LIT-771](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-771.md), are consistent with it without testing it. Whether human chains do is [QUESTION-137](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-137.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-163](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-163.md) v5 | Colour naming lies near the bottleneck bound | Zaslavsky, Kemp, Regier & Tishby (2018), [LIT-810](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-810.md), read in [NOTE-631](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-631.md): treating a colour lexicon as an encoder from Gaussian perceptual meanings to words, the World Color Survey languages and English lie near the IB curve of [LIT-338](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-338.md) at β ≈ 1.03, beat hue-rotated variants of themselves, and their soft, partly inconsistent naming is what IB optima look like. It does not show that languages are driven to the bound by any process, and the need distribution that makes the fit best is estimated from the naming data themselves. | Active |
| [THEORY-166](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-166.md) v4 | Question-order equality doesn't favour quantum | Wang, Solloway, Shiffrin & Busemeyer (2014), [LIT-795](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-795.md), on the QQ equality derived in [LIT-834](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-834.md): across the 66 Pew surveys of 2001-2011 that varied the order of two questions, question order shifts the answers (p = 0.0004) but not the probability that the two answers agree (p = 0.4625). The Lüders projection model predicts this without parameters, by a one-line identity. A classical model with order events can be built to satisfy the equality, and [LIT-264](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-264.md) shows that data meeting it are noncontextual, so it is evidence for a constraint on order effects, not for nonclassical probability or contextuality. A preregistered test with a constrained classical rival is [QUESTION-210](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-210.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-172](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-172.md) v5 | Listeners infer speakers choose by informativeness | Frank & Goodman (2012), [LIT-821](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-821.md), read in [NOTE-634](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-634.md): a parameter-free Bayesian listener inverting a size-principle speaker, with a separately measured salience prior, matches mean listener bets over seven context types at r = .99 (.87 without the 0 and 100 predictions), while salience alone correlates at r = .19. Bergen, Goodman & Levy (2012), [LIT-809](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-809.md), read in [NOTE-613](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-613.md): with novel signals and no conventions, listeners read the signal as the object its alternative did not name, and lexical uncertainty derives Horn's mapping. Goodman & Frank (2016), [LIT-816](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-816.md), states the framework. Shown for artificial games with given alternatives, by fits of condition means with no rival fitted; a test against named rivals on trial-level data is [QUESTION-209](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-209.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-208](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-208.md) | Agency needs no cognition; AI is a new kind | Floridi (2025), [LIT-897](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-897.md), read in [NOTE-702](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-702.md), with the criteria taken from Floridi & Sanders (2004), [LIT-898](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-898.md). In the record's reading, agency comes in kinds. All of them share interactivity, and the richer ones add graded autonomy and adaptability. The kinds are told apart by origin, mechanism and where their goals come from, not by intelligence. AI is computational agency with data-driven learning, serving goals set by humans, with no intelligence or mental states. Proposed: the paper assumes that AI is an agent, does not argue for this thesis over its rival, asserts that AI lacks intelligence, and never states the level of abstraction its comparison uses. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-220](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-220.md) v5 | Self-maintenance grounds intrinsic function | Bickhard (2000), [LIT-1029](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1029.md), read in [NOTE-729](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-729.md). Function is contribution to a far-from-equilibrium system's own persistence; the asymmetry between persisting and decaying gives function and dysfunction, always relative to the system served, so a parasite's gut serves the parasite and harms the host. A candle flame has functions in this sense. Representation arrives with recursive self-maintenance: a system that picks its next interaction by how it has differentiated its environment implicitly predicates that the interaction will succeed, and can find the predication false. Proposed: a conceptual account, with no model, whose account of having a function (and so of malfunction) is deferred to another paper. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-245](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-245.md) v4 | Prefrontal cortex carries category, not identity | Cogitate Consortium, Ferrante et al. (2025), [LIT-973](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-973.md), read in [NOTE-812](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-812.md). In iEEG and fMRI, with Bayesian support for the nulls, and against a positive control, prefrontal cortex held category but no identity or orientation, and none of 655 prefrontal electrodes showed the onset-and-offset response GNWT predicted. It does not show these dimensions were unaccessed, or that prefrontal cortex lacks them in other signals: high gamma and BOLD only, no single units, and every image was seen. | Active |
| [THEORY-255](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-255.md) v4 | Meet and join can't overextend concepts | Aerts (2009), [LIT-934](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-934.md), Theorem 9 and §§2.2–3.3, read in full in [NOTE-808](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-808.md). The impossibility is a proof, and it needs only that membership is monotone in the subspace. The fits that place the k-type deviations in a tilted subspace lattice and the ∆-type ones in an emergent sector are models with free parameters, not tests. Negation appears only as the orthocomplement used to derive the conjunction model from the disjunction model; no negated concept is measured. | Active |
| [THEORY-261](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-261.md) v3 | SDM capacity scales with hard locations | Kanerva (1992), [LIT-921](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-921.md), §§3.5–3.7, read in full in [NOTE-779](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-779.md), after Jaeckel (1989a). An approximate derivation for uniform random data and exact retrieval cues. It does not cover noisy cues, which lower capacity, or clustered data, which the uniform design handles badly, and it does not contain the critical-distance analysis that is sometimes attributed to it. | Active |
| [THEORY-272](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-272.md) v4 | Hopfield nets recall up to about 0.15N | Hopfield (1982), [LIT-918](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-918.md), read in full in [NOTE-819](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-819.md). The energy descent is derived for symmetric couplings; everything quantitative, including the 0.15N figure, the basin width and the merging distance, is simulation at N = 30 and 100. It does not say that spurious states come only from overload: they appear at a low load too. Nor does it say anything about addressed memory. | Active |
| [THEORY-330](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-330.md) | People choose their reward-optimal memory load | Howes, Duggan, Kalidindi, Tseng and Lewis (2016), [LIT-1062](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1062.md), read in [NOTE-882](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-882.md). Participants copied names shown one at a time from a mock email to a calendar. Each person's best list length in their own data predicted 55% and 46% of their choices, against 8–17% for the neighbouring lengths (N = 40 and 20). An exponential points schedule raised chosen length (6.99 against 5.07); forfeiting the whole trial on one error did not (5.00 against 5.05). 13 of 60 persistently chose a non-optimal length. There is no look-up and no model: the prediction is each person's empirical argmax. Lieder and Griffiths' description of it as a memorize-or-look-up trade ([LIT-1071](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1071.md)) does not fit the task. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-334](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-334.md) v3 | Block copiers look back rather than memorize | Ballard, Hayhoe, Pook and Rao (1997), [LIT-1075](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1075.md), read in [NOTE-883](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-883.md). Fixations are modelled as pointers that bind a program's variable to a place in the world, so that only the task-relevant feature is fetched, just before use. In block copying, look-model, pick-up, look-model, drop was the commonest cycle (about 43% of cycles), at about 3 s a block against 1.5 s from memory; 70° separation cut looks from 1.3 to 1.0 per block, and one-colour patterns to 0.7. A colour changed mid-saccade mostly went unnoticed and cost time only once colour was held. The "carrying cost" of working memory is inferred from choice, not measured, and what is left in the world is raw input, not a computed result. Promoted 2026-10-20 on the observations alone (ADR-047 v3). | Active |
| [THEORY-335](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-335.md) v2 | Selective accessibility's key step is unmeasured | Strack & Mussweiler (1997), [LIT-1064](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1064.md), read in [NOTE-877](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-877.md), proposed the account and showed, in three small studies, that with the anchor number fixed the effect depends on whether the knowledge used to compare applies to the later estimate, and that plausible anchors slow the comparison and speed the estimate. Accessibility is inferred, never measured. Harris et al. (2019), [LIT-1067](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1067.md), read in [NOTE-876](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-876.md), repeated the recognition test (lexical decision, once continuous identification) of the accessibility step (Mussweiler & Strack 2000a, not held) five times at N = 128: anchoring was large and recognition of anchor-consistent words never moved (BF01 ≈ 21), but the same tasks missed direct picture priming. So the direct evidence is removed, not reversed; the account is neither refuted nor shown. Mussweiler & Strack 1999 ([LIT-1078](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1078.md)) is Unavailable. | Active |
| [THEORY-336](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-336.md) v2 | Ideal-observer stages locate perceptual losses | Geisler (2011), [LIT-1055](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1055.md), read in [NOTE-870](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-870.md). A review that defines the ideal observer as optimal "given the available information and any specified constraints", and writes it as an expected-utility argmax over the posterior given the stimulus S or a constrained representation Z = g(S;θ). Constraints are added one at a time (optics, receptor sampling and noise, ganglion-cell summation), and human performance that parallels the retinal-stage ideal while falling below it is read as loss in central factors. The empirical parts are the review's account of studies the record has not read. The review gives no formula for efficiency and no notion of an optimum over a restricted class of computations. | Active |
| [THEORY-337](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-337.md) | Comparative anchors pull estimates, and it lasts | Harris et al. (2019), [LIT-1067](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1067.md), read in [NOTE-876](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-876.md), and Strack & Mussweiler (1997), [LIT-1064](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1064.md), read in [NOTE-877](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-877.md). In five preregistered experiments (N = 128 each) on temperatures and car prices, estimates after a high anchor exceeded those after a low one every time (d ≈ 0.85–1.39), with 40 to 70 word-recognition trials between the comparison and the estimate. Strack and Mussweiler's three small studies show the same effect, and that it can shrink or reverse when the knowledge used to compare does not apply to the estimate. This is the effect, not its mechanism: why the estimate moves is [THEORY-335](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-335.md)'s question and is not settled. | Active |
| [THEORY-339](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-339.md) | Probability judgments reuse earlier answers | Dasgupta, Schulz, Goodman and Gershman (2018), [LIT-1074](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1074.md), read in [NOTE-875](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-875.md); Gershman and Goodman (2014), [LIT-1056](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1056.md), read in [NOTE-886](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-886.md); Dasgupta and Gershman (2021), [LIT-1077](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1077.md), read in [NOTE-865](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-865.md). In five small online experiments, an earlier answer shapes a later one only when the later query can use it, and errors in the first carry into the second. The authors call this amortized inference, reuse of past computation bought at a cost in bias. The speed benefit is shown once (median log-RT facilitation, n ≈ 50 per order) and otherwise assumed; storage and retrieval are free in the models; the 2021 review adds stale cached values from the planning literature, second-hand. No paper prices when reuse pays or touches stores outside the head. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-343](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-343.md) | Offloading tracks felt demand, not benefit | Risko & Gilbert (2016), [LIT-1059](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1059.md), read in [NOTE-887](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-887.md). A review: in choice/no-choice studies of rotated displays, delayed intentions and short-term memory, spontaneous offloading rises with internal demand, but it also occurs where it gives no gain (writing items down about 40% of the time at a two-item load already at ceiling), rises with lower confidence after ability is controlled, and differs between displays of equal measured demand. Expecting to have a result stored externally went with poorer memory for it. The review reports no effect sizes, the cited studies were not read, and its metacognitive model is an unformalised box diagram; the drift toward external reliance is a prediction, not a finding. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-346](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-346.md) | Costlier access shifts reliance to memory | Gray, Sims, Fu and Schoelles (2006), [LIT-1073](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1073.md), read in [NOTE-868](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-868.md), and Gray and Fu (2004), [LIT-1058](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1058.md), read in [NOTE-864](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-864.md). Adding a click to reach on-screen show information cut how often it was checked, and checks of finished settings came from memory. Lockouts of 0 to 3,200 ms on a Blocks World pattern cut looks and raised blocks placed per look, with linear trends. An ideal performer model with ACT-R memory equations and Q-learning on time alone fits four measures. That the control system has no bias toward the world is argued, not tested against a rival model. Errors in the 2004 study differed only against a group that memorized under several other changes, and the 2006 model has no wrong retrievals, no precomputation, no reuse across trials and no staleness. | Active |
| [THEORY-351](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-351.md) v2 | Speed bugs let the cockpit remember speeds | Hutchins (1995), [LIT-1066](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1066.md), read in [NOTE-867](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-867.md). A stylized task analysis of one airline's MD-80 procedure, informed by observation but reporting no measurements. The speed-card booklet, filtered by the displayed gross weight, is the system's long-term memory; the values pass through speech to bugs on two airspeed indicators, and on approach the pilots judge the needle's nearness to a bug instead of recalling and reading speeds. The paper concludes that the memory is "not made primarily of pilot memory". It analyses only success, for an anticipated, mandated and invariant task with a few values needed in a fixed order, so it says nothing about search for one item among many under a deadline. Cognition in the Wild ([LIT-1060](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1060.md)) is Unavailable. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-355](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-355.md) | Arranging surroundings replaces internal search | Kirsh (1995), [LIT-1076](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1076.md), read in [NOTE-871](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-871.md), and Kirsh (1996), [LIT-1057](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1057.md), read in [NOTE-872](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-872.md). From video of cooks, assemblers and baggers and from informal observation, Kirsh classifies arrangements that simplify choice, perception and internal computation, frames their savings in search-complexity terms, and ties set-up cost to the number of choice points an arrangement serves. The 1996 paper adds a verbal investment rule with an interest factor for risk, one risk being that the change is not still present later, and upkeep against scatter. Neither paper gives a cost model or a measured saving; the 1995 paper says the savings do not "in general" admit meaningful quantitative estimation, and the 1996 paper puts mental cost outside its formalism. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-358](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-358.md) v2 | Conjunction search is serial, feature search not | Treisman and Gelade (1980), [LIT-1082](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1082.md), read in [NOTE-897](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-897.md). With coloured letters on cards of 1 to 30 or 36 items, a blue letter or an S among brown Ts and green Xs was found at 3.8 and 2.5 ms per item, and a green T among the same distractors at 28.7 ms per item when present and 67.1 when absent, linear and in the ratio of a scan that stops at the first find; 13 sessions of practice did not change it. The paper reads the contrast as feature integration: conjunction structure, not similarity, makes search serial. That reading is contested by the similarity account of Duncan and Humphreys ([LIT-1081](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1081.md)), which the record could not obtain, and it does not follow that any item unique in one attribute pops out in a real pile. | Active |
| [THEORY-359](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-359.md) | Resource-rational analysis rederives heuristics | Lieder & Griffiths (2020; online 2019), [LIT-1071](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1071.md), read in [NOTE-873](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-873.md). Resource rationality picks the heuristic that maximizes expected utility of its result minus the expected opportunity cost of the time and resources it uses (Eq. 3), averaged over environments consistent with what is known (Eq. 4), and a five-step method derives process models from it. The support is a review of others' models recast in this frame, with numbers from those studies. The authors offer optimality as a methodological device, not a claim about people, and the method lets constraints be refitted to data. The objective is per episode, with no terms for storing, retrieving or reusing a result, or for its going stale. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-360](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-360.md) v2 | Tetris players rotate early and probe the wall | Kirsh and Maglio (1994), [LIT-1054](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1054.md), read in [NOTE-878](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-878.md), with Kirsh (1995), [LIT-1076](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1076.md), read in [NOTE-871](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-871.md). In Tetris keystroke data, pieces are rotated more than plan-then-act would need, rotation starts by 400–600 ms, and a translate-to-wall check precedes longer drops. The authors define an epistemic action as one whose primary function is to cut the space, time or unreliability of the agent's own computation, and argue these moves are of that kind. The saving is argued from a three-player pilot comparing physical with mental rotation, not measured in performance. The trade is offloading at the moment of use, once, with nothing stored; the paper sets itself against caching. Promoted 2026-10-20 on the timing and Table 1 alone (ADR-047 v3); the epistemic-action reading is held as THEORY-823. | Active |
| [THEORY-402](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-402.md) | Collective intelligence is modular bounded compute | Pilgrim et al. (2025), [LIT-046](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-046.md), read in [NOTE-055](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-055.md), with Dreyer et al. (2024), [LIT-075](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-075.md) ([NOTE-040](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-040.md)), as its clearest instance. The paper offers a four-dimensional resource inventory, a catalogue of constraints and a mapping to mechanisms, and calls the known forms of collective intelligence "aspects of a single unifying principle". [NOTE-055](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-055.md) judges it a vocabulary, not a derivation: the resources have no metric, so the framework cannot say in advance when costs outweigh gains, and its "predictions" are research questions. Filed Proposed as the account the vocabulary states. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-433](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-433.md) | Replace machine thought with the imitation game | Turing (1950), [LIT-394](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-394.md), read in [NOTE-355](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-355.md). The imitation game is offered in place of a definition of thinking, not as a test of it, and Turing says he has "no very convincing arguments of a positive nature". The account's force is the other-minds parity of §6.4, which assumes, as §2 states and does not argue, that the machine's best strategy is to answer as a man would; a machine built to imitate human output is the case that assumption does not cover. It makes no claim about consciousness. Proposed, and a rival of Block's psychologism. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-436](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-436.md) | Pain is a functional state, not a brain state | Putnam (1967), [LIT-396](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-396.md), recorded as Skimmed in [NOTE-335](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-335.md) from a course excerpt of the 1975 reprint, which carries the four-clause hypothesis verbatim; the original is Unavailable here. Proposed, and resting on that excerpt and on a result discussed throughout the literature the record holds. Clause (1) is empty by Putnam's own admission, since everything is a probabilistic automaton under some description, and clause (3), the anti-nesting condition, is introduced with one motive, to rule out swarms of bees. The argument against the brain-state view is comparative plausibility, not evidence. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-438](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-438.md) | Deep nets' understanding is real but fractured | Freeborn (2026), [LIT-131](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-131.md), read in [NOTE-123](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-123.md). The Fractured Understanding Hypothesis is argued from four small demonstrations and cited literature, with no test of how common the five features are. The abstract names three features and §7.5 five. The paper also applies its own criteria inconsistently: its Othello verdict uses post hoc probes that it excludes from the agent. The definition of understanding it rests on is an explication, not a finding. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-454](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-454.md) v2 | Percepts enter cognition only when recoded | Block (2024), [LIT-649](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-649.md), read in [NOTE-498](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-498.md): the précis of his 2023 book, not the book. The main thesis is stated and its arguments are in the book, unread here. The working-memory half is the update: nine cited lines of evidence that working-memory representations differ from perceptual ones and are task-dependent abstractions (moderate). The rereading of the workspace as conceptualisation rather than consciousness is asserted, not argued against the consciousness reading. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-458](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-458.md) v2 | Sense of ownership and agency come apart | Gallagher (2000), [LIT-453](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-453.md), read in [NOTE-377](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-377.md) from the preprint. A review with no new results: the dissociation and the comparator account are reported from Frith, Haggard and others, and the link to the immunity principle is Campbell's argument, adopted and left conditional. It is about the minimal self, not the narrative self, for which the review's own proposal is two paragraphs. It does not say which minimal self, embodied or reflective, the analysis concerns. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-460](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-460.md) | LLM consciousness barriers are mostly removable | Chalmers (2023), [LIT-411](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-411.md), read in full in [NOTE-345](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-345.md). A classification of objections as temporary or permanent, argued by naming simple systems that have each feature. The credences that follow, under 10% for current models and 25% or more for conscious extended models within a decade, are illustrative by the author's warning, multiply stipulated factors under a disclaimed independence assumption, and depend on "mainstream assumptions". Biology is set aside with a reference to earlier work. It adds no evidence about any model. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-461](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-461.md) | Chatbots' bodily self-reports are untrue | Roberts (2026), [LIT-207](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-207.md), read in [NOTE-157](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-157.md). The anti-realist half is a valid conditional whose antecedent, moderate embodied cognition, is assumed at prima facie strength. It covers body-dependent states only; footnote 8 allows realism about the chatbot as a disembodied thinker, so belief and reasoning are untouched. The fictionalist half shows the attitude permissible and apt, not required, and offers no evidence that users hold it. It is not a general denial that chatbots have minds. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-462](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-462.md) v2 | Monotonic logic can't represent displaced defaults | Minsky (1974), the frames memo, [LIT-410](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-410.md), read in [NOTE-337](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-337.md). Its appendix argues that "logistic" systems fail for commonsense on five counts, of which monotonicity is a correct observation about classical logic. That no repair is possible is asserted ("I think such attempts will continue to fail"), and consistency being undesirable is argued by analogy. The reading says the memo is a source of hypotheses, not evidence; this account takes from it only the half that holds by definition and marks the rest as the memo's claim. Active as the definitional half and a report of how the memo supports the rest; the further claim is THEORY-1239, Proposed. | Active |
| [THEORY-471](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-471.md) | Mental states aren't machine-table states | Block & Fodor (1972), [LIT-641](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-641.md), read in [NOTE-491](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-491.md). Five independent arguments against the machine-state identity theory, each with a stated escape that keeps functionalism: dispositions with no occurrent state, simultaneous states, too-fine individuation, productivity and constituent structure. They refute the machine-table clause, not functionalism. The paper's remaining argument (its third), inverted or absent qualia, is the only one aimed at functionalism broadly, and it is explicitly prima facie. | Active |
| [THEORY-472](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-472.md) v4 | Size principle follows from informative speech | Frank, Goodman, Lai and Tenenbaum (2009), [LIT-824](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-824.md), read in full in [NOTE-627](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-627.md). The derivation (utility −D_KL from intended to literal meaning gives P(w) ∝ \|w\|^(−α) for a point referent) is a proof under its assumptions. Learners' bets track the parameter-free inversion at r = .93 on condition means (700 web participants); speakers' tag-word use in free descriptions correlates at r = .19, .51 without colour terms and .02 for them. In these displays the informative-speaker learner and a plain size-principle learner coincide by construction, so the fit does not show that learners reason about the speaker. | Active |
| [THEORY-475](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-475.md) | Hierarchical Bayes recovers DDM parameters best | Wiecki, Sofer & Frank (2013), [LIT-563](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-563.md), read in [NOTE-466](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-466.md). Experiment 1 gives the lowest trimmed recovery error for HB on every parameter, and HB beat ML on the same data sets in every condition. Experiments 2–3 report more power to detect drift differences and trial-wise covariate effects, but HB was judged by a posterior-interval test and the others by t-tests, and the clean comparison was omitted. All data were generated from DDMs, with sz = st = 0. It is the standard partial-pooling result shown for one model family, not a test of the DDM. | Active |
| [THEORY-489](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-489.md) | Iterated learners converge to positive linear | Kalish, Griffiths & Lewandowsky (2007), [LIT-820](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-820.md), read in [NOTE-616](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-616.md). 288 participants in 32 nine-generation chains, four starting conditions. 28 families converged to a positive linear function; 3 converged to the negative linear one and 1 had not converged. The bias was taken from earlier studies, not measured on these learners, and stationarity was not established. It supports the claim that human transmission chains settle on what learners favour in this task, not that they reach the Bayesian prior, and it cannot tell sampling learners from MAP learners. | Active |
| [THEORY-500](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-500.md) | Somatic markers prune options before reasoning | Damasio (1996), [LIT-384](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-384.md), read in [NOTE-332](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-332.md), the somatic marker hypothesis stated by its author; Bechara, Damasio, Tranel and Damasio (1997), [LIT-383](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-383.md), read in [NOTE-331](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-331.md), the experiment it is usually cited for. The robust result is a group difference: in the gambling task all 10 controls and none of 6 ventromedial patients developed anticipatory skin conductance responses. That controls chose well before they knew, and that the marker causes the choice, is not carried by the statistics. The mechanism is argued, not observed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-512](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-512.md) | Extended mind can reach belief, not consciousness | Chalmers (2019), [LIT-415](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-415.md), read in [NOTE-356](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-356.md), and his foreword to Clark's book (2008), [LIT-421](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-421.md), read in [NOTE-369](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-369.md). The 1998 thesis is satisfied by wired-in "extended circuits" that its critics accept, so the controversial thesis is constitution through perception and action. The perception-action boundary is then the strongest objection, met by revisionism, not refuted. Consciousness does not extend this way, on an imported criterion (direct availability, "not mediated by other mental states") and on the absence of any working twin case. Both halves are proposals defended against a few cases; the criterion is the author's earlier correlate of consciousness, not an argument made here. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-520](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-520.md) | Interaction can gain autonomy of its own | De Jaegher and Di Paolo (2007), [LIT-571](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-571.md), read in [NOTE-456](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-456.md). A conceptual account built on coordination dynamics, with illustrative evidence: the corridor, charades, mother–infant timing and the perceptual-crossing experiments of Auvray et al., reported, not new. [NOTE-456](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-456.md) declined a THEORY because the source carries no claim beyond its definition. The claim with some support is the perceptual-crossing one; the autonomy of the interaction is a definition, and the implications are called "speculative at this stage" by the authors. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-528](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-528.md) | Embedded cognition explains extended cases | Rupert (2004), [LIT-422](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-422.md), read in [NOTE-343](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-343.md). The past-endorsement dilemma is strong: without it, directory assistance makes Otto believe every listed number; with it, the organism's endorsement is the final authority. The memory comparisons are moderate: the internal side is cited research, the external side is thought experiment, and no experiment on an external store is run or cited. The step from "different fine-grained kinds" to "no useful coarse kind" is a challenge plus conservatism. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-529](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-529.md) | Representation is efficient transmission | Martínez (2025), [LIT-149](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-149.md), read in [NOTE-165](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-165.md): a position paper with no new theorem or data. Its sharpest point is a standard result: by the data-processing inequality, mutual information about a car/no-car decision can only fall from retina to IT, so a mutual-information criterion would place the decision at the earliest stage; explicitness is better read as ease of decoding. The rest is a proposal supported by selected examples. Complexity has no operational measure, teleofunctions are needed to fix the distortion measure or every system is efficient for some loss, and misrepresentation and engineered systems are not addressed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-538](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-538.md) | Belief is intentional-stance predictability | Dennett, "True Believers", [LIT-398](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-398.md), read in [NOTE-353](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-353.md) in the revised text of 1987/1997. The criterion is substrate-neutral and silent on experience. Its adverbs are not quantified, the lectern is excluded only by gain over a baseline the essay leaves informal, and the Martian argument is an intuition pump that assumes the intentional patterns are not captured physically. "Most beliefs are true" rests on a way of counting beliefs Dennett doubts exists. Proposed, and a rival of both Block's psychologism and Searle's causal-powers account. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-541](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-541.md) | Hand-built representations give away the answer | Chalmers, French & Hofstadter (1992), [LIT-414](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-414.md), read in [NOTE-359](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-359.md) from the preprint, with Burns's review of Fluid Concepts (1995), [LIT-457](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-457.md), read in [NOTE-375](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-375.md). The BACON critique is strong; the SME critique moderate, with no alternative encoding run; the two arguments against a representation module informal. Burns turns the charges on Copycat: its Slipnet holds the domain's relevant relations, and the symbol-grounding objection to SME applies to it equally. Nothing is measured in either text. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-542](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-542.md) | Inferring speaker intent improves word learning | Frank, Goodman & Tenenbaum (2009), [LIT-815](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-815.md), read in [NOTE-611](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-611.md). On about twenty minutes of video from two dyads, annotated by the authors, the intentional model's lexicon scores precision .67 and F .55 against .06–.15 and .10–.22 for five baselines. The behavioural fits are qualitative, the baselines also produce mutual exclusivity, and the Baldwin case supplies the intention rather than inferring it. The reading said no THEORY, because the findings are specific to a small corpus and the record held nothing they correct; this account is filed Proposed for that reason. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-545](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-545.md) | Quantum concept model is classical underneath | Aerts & Gabora (2005), Parts II and I, [LIT-312](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-312.md) and [LIT-340](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-340.md), read in [NOTE-299](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-299.md) and [NOTE-294](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-294.md). The structural facts are checks of the published model, not of the authors' prose: contexts are sums of basis projectors, counts are chosen to match rounded frequencies, and the authors call the result a "quantization" of a set-theoretical model. Part I's mark of non-classicality (eq. 19) is met by Boolean projection lattices too, and its lattice structure is supposed, not derived. The model as printed is also infeasible in two cells. It does not say that no quantum model of concepts does better. | Active |
| [THEORY-547](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-547.md) v2 | Idealized LMs track narrative, not truth | Bottou & Schölkopf (2023), [LIT-178](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-178.md), read in [NOTE-102](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-102.md): an essay offering imagery, with no evidence beyond one Vicuna-13b transcript pair. For the "perfect language model" it defines, insensitivity to truth follows from the definition. That deployed chat models share it is assumed, and the essay's own §2 leaves open whether alignment can turn a fiction machine into a verification machine. It credits the machine with knowledge of what makes sense in the story, denies it truth-directedness and intention, and never uses the word "sycophancy". | Active |
| [THEORY-558](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-558.md) | Moral judgment is intuition; reasoning post hoc | Haidt (2001), [LIT-511](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-511.md), read in [NOTE-403](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-403.md): the social intuitionist model. Its case rests mostly on non-moral evidence about automaticity, motivated reasoning and confabulation, carried over by argument. Its direct moral evidence is that harmless taboo violations are condemned and that affect predicts the condemnation better than perceived harm. The author calls it "a plausible alternative", not "an established fact". The disgust manipulations that were its direct causal evidence were later disputed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-563](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-563.md) v2 | Consciousness is a coarse real pattern | Taylor (2024), [LIT-461](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-461.md), read in full in [NOTE-379](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-379.md). An interpretation of Dennett offered as consistent, explicitly not as correct or as what Dennett meant. Its argument for indeterminacy in masking rests on Dennett's idealised description of the cases, which Taylor calls "somewhat simplistic". It does not say which real pattern consciousness is, or what makes a real pattern a conscious one rather than a belief pattern. Filed as the account the reading states, at the strength the reading gives it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-564](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-564.md) v2 | Model can grow its own structure, unreliably | Smith, Schwartenbeck, Parr and Friston (2020), [LIT-615](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-615.md), read in [NOTE-485](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-485.md). Expansion works in the toy domain over eight runs per condition, and only for novel stimuli. Reduction is the weak half: over 100 runs, the true number of concepts won in 45–80% of runs for four to seven, never for two or three, and in every run when the likelihood was given. Table 1 is the record's only measurement of how often reduction picks the generating structure when the parent model was itself learned. One initialisation; eight concepts, six binary features. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-570](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-570.md) | Emotions are resource selections, like thinking | Minsky (2006), The Emotion Machine, [LIT-432](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-432.md), read in [NOTE-348](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-348.md) from the author's 2005 draft. A design argued from examples, thought experiments and the author's own AI programs, with no experiment; Minsky marks several parts as his untested conjecture. It disagrees directly with the body-state views of emotion and of feeling. On Elliot it proposes the reverse causal order to Damasio's, with no evidence offered. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-573](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-573.md) | Pooled fluency signals help unify experience | Winkielman, Ziembowicz & Nowak (2015), [LIT-190](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-190.md), read in full in [NOTE-146](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-146.md). An opinion piece whose main evidence is the authors' own three experiments (Ziembowicz et al. 2013), summarised without statistics and not read by the record. The authors state that direct evidence is still needed that the effects run through changed experience and that its integration is causal. No study cited measures unity of experience. The LIT is itself Proposed; this account carries its promotion condition. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-577](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-577.md) | Hard-problem judgments are an easy problem | Chalmers (2018), [LIT-425](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-425.md), read in full in [NOTE-354](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-354.md). The meta-problem follows from the physical explicability of behaviour; the challenge is a constraint argued from it, "not a knockdown argument". It assumes that a zero-Φ simulation has the same intuitions on a functional reading, which an IIT theorist can deny. The paper's own favoured solution, opaque introspective models attributing primitive relations of acquaintance, is "closer to a fleshed-out explanandum" than an explanation, and the data the programme needs mostly do not exist. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-579](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-579.md) v2 | Constantly used external stores can hold beliefs | Clark & Chalmers (1998), [LIT-097](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-097.md), read in [NOTE-180](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-180.md), with Clark's reply to the critics (2005), [LIT-403](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-403.md), read in [NOTE-363](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-363.md). Otto's notebook plays for him the role Inga's memory plays for her, so on role-functionalism it carries his standing belief, and Twin Otto, a duplicate from the skin in, believes otherwise. The constitutive step is carried by role-functionalism, the parity sentence and explanatory simplicity, none of them defended; the four coupling features mark a clear case and are explicitly not necessary and sufficient. Proposed: the step from causal coupling to parthood is the open point. The thesis is about vehicles of standing beliefs, not about consciousness. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-582](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-582.md) | Coupling alone doesn't make cognition extended | Adams & Aizawa (2001), [LIT-438](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-438.md), read in [NOTE-368](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-368.md), and their reply to Clark (2010, read from a draft), [LIT-455](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-455.md), read in [NOTE-380](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-380.md). A thermostat's bimetallic strip, the kidney's filtration and a nerve at a neuromuscular junction are each coupled to more than themselves, and their processes do not extend. The 2010 text names the inference the "coupling-constitution fallacy". The point is that coupling does not entail parthood. It is not shown that coupling never accompanies parthood, nor that the extended-mind authors relied on coupling alone. | Active |
| [THEORY-588](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-588.md) | Separate lemma stage fails polysynthesis, idioms | Krauska and Lau (2023), [LIT-031](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-031.md), read in full in [NOTE-029](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-029.md). A Hypothesis and Theory article with no new data and no implementation. Its diagnosis of named models (Levelt, the Consensus Model, lexically sized increments, treelets) is strong as textual analysis; the case that they fail on Inuktitut, Vietnamese collocations and Hiaki suppletion is argued from a few examples each, and Eberhard et al. are conceded to handle Hiaki in part. The 8-stage replacement model and its aphasia predictions are a verbal sketch, and this account does not rest on them. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-591](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-591.md) | Cognition is contingently bound to the brain | Adams & Aizawa (2001), [LIT-438](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-438.md), read in [NOTE-368](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-368.md), restated against Clark in 2010, [LIT-455](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-455.md), read in [NOTE-380](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-380.md) from a draft. Both marks are assumed: the first on a claimed consensus, the second on how mature sciences individuate kinds. The authors grant the parity principle and that cognition could extend; the claim is that it does not. The "no science of tool use" half is offered as a bet. Rupert, the other critic, rejects the derived-content argument as question-begging. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-593](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-593.md) v3 | Perceptual learning can reshape individuation | Ivy & Mroczko-Wąsowicz (2025), [LIT-099](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-099.md), read in [NOTE-150](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-150.md). A conceptual proposal: a frame is installed by learning, often top-down, and then runs as a perceiver-specific structural principle of objecthood, so the system-level and episode-level questions about cognitive penetration come apart. The support is others' results reread through the concept, and one eye-tracking study of the authors'. The paper does not say what "bottom-up" means once priors sit in early processing, calls a frame "a specific top-down prediction" in §3.iii, and shows different weightings, not different objects. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-596](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-596.md) | Believers are rational-system idealisations | Dennett (1971), [LIT-440](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-440.md), read in [NOTE-350](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-350.md), and his reply to Stich (1980), [LIT-456](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-456.md), read in [NOTE-371](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-371.md). Belief ascription presupposes optimal design relative to goals, so "a false belief system is a conceptual impossibility" and, following Quine, the evidence for ascribing p is the best evidence against ascribing a contradictory q. In 1980 Dennett concedes the price: the intentional system, and the person, is "an unrealizable idealization". Argued from the logic of ascription and from evolution by assertion; no data. It is a claim about what ascription requires, not about what is in heads. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-601](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-601.md) | Philosophy majors score higher, not shown causal | Prinzing & Vazquez (2025), [LIT-155](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-155.md), read in full in [NOTE-167](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-167.md). HERI/CIRP freshman–senior data on 649,511 students at 804 institutions, 4,843 philosophy majors. Selection is real (SAT Verbal OR 1.57, SAT Math none). Baseline-adjusted mixed models and an IPTW check agree on the verbal and logical-test advantage and on its absence for quantitative tests. All test scores are self-reported, the SAT is an imperfect baseline for the LSAT, and nothing rules out faster verbal growth or harder test preparation among those who choose philosophy, so the paper's causal title is not part of this account. | Active |
| [THEORY-603](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-603.md) v2 | Iowa task doesn't show pre-aware advantage | Bechara, Damasio, Tranel & Damasio (1997), [LIT-383](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-383.md), read in [NOTE-331](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-331.md). The robust results are the group difference in anticipatory SCRs (Fisher's exact, one-sided P < 0.001) and the insufficiency of stated knowledge in three patients. The abstract's "before they realized which strategy worked best" and "before they knew" outrun notes 8 and 9: the pre-hunch choice preference was not significant, and the pre-hunch SCR effect reported is group × period, with no bad-versus-good deck test. Nothing here shows that the SCR, or what it indexes, causes the choice. | Active |
| [THEORY-608](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-608.md) | Ant groups improve with size; humans don't | Dreyer et al. (2024), [LIT-075](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-075.md), read in [NOTE-040](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-040.md). Large ant groups (n = 28) reach about 90–100% success by 400 corridor widths, small groups (n = 48) about 50%. Restricted human groups do 32% worse than individuals' median, talking groups 7% better. There are no inferential statistics. The ant persistence mechanism is supported by collision data and a model whose carrier numbers fall short of calibration; the human majority vote (greediness P = 0.2) is tuned by eye, and "follow a random leader" rests on unrecorded observation. One ant species, one puzzle, one human population. | Active |
| [THEORY-609](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-609.md) v2 | Finite-state automata can't ground computation | Chalmers (1996), [LIT-404](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-404.md), read in [NOTE-342](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-342.md) from the author's HTML copy. The failure of Putnam's construction and the clock-and-dial and input-memory theorems are constructive proofs given the definitions, so FSA-functionalism "still almost reduces to behaviorism". That a combinatorial-state automaton can be implemented only by the right fine-grained causal structure is a sketch: the obvious blind construction grows by a factor of n per step, and that every construction does is asserted. Logically possible false implementations and the one-region-per-component condition are left open by the author. | Active |
| [THEORY-616](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-616.md) v2 | LLM attitudes belong to instances, not models | Goldstein & Lederman (2025), [LIT-206](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-206.md), read in [NOTE-138](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-138.md) from the preprint. Conditional on objective interpretationism, which the authors do not defend. The instance thesis is moderately argued; the presumptive case for attitudes rests on a tractability comparison never operationalised or measured; HHH+0 is "provisional", and its discriminating test is a conjecture. All the empirical support is second-hand and qualitative. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-636](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-636.md) | Desire judgments track intentionality under luck | Quillien (2026), [LIT-132](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-132.md), read in [NOTE-092](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-092.md). Three Prolific studies (N = 198, 673, 142; ratings 1–7). Causation is the strongest predictor of intentionality (standardized β .46, .56, .53, against know-how .33, .20, .27 and probability-raising .14, .16, .10), and a pre-registered Knowledge × Process interaction predicted by the causal account holds (F(1, 423) = 32). The evidence is correlational, the mediation exploratory and partial (64%, 45%, 49%), and in the neutral Kraemer vignette causation shows no effect where intentionality does. The "model" is verbal; robustness is never measured. | Active |
| [THEORY-638](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-638.md) | Running a program isn't understanding | Searle (1980), [LIT-400](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-400.md), read in [NOTE-349](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-349.md) (target article only). The room is a full implementation run by a person, and his first-person verdict is read as the system's. The decisive step against the systems reply ("the system is just a part of him") is asserted, not shown, and which causal powers matter is left empirical. The argument is about understanding and intentionality, not consciousness, and it grants that machines, including artifacts with the brain's causal powers, could think. Proposed; Dennett's intentional strategy is its rival. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-646](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-646.md) | Rep skepticism doesn't motivate fictionalism | Drayson (2025), [LIT-112](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-112.md), read in [NOTE-117](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-117.md), against Toon's Mind As Metaphor (2023). Toon's negative argument needs "committed to internal, intentional, causal attitudes ⇒ committed to RTM", which non-representational functionalism (Lewis, Putnam, Loar) makes false; and his metasemantic case against inner representation mistakes one motivation for RTM for part of it. His positive argument faces a dilemma: a merely behavioural overall state gives fictionalism no causal advantage, and a causal one is a reason to identify it with the belief. It argues against two motivations, assumes fictionalism coherent, and sketches the functionalist alternative by citation in one paragraph. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-662](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-662.md) | Fluency is inferred processing precision | Brouillet and Friston (2023), [LIT-957](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-957.md), read in [NOTE-785](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-785.md). A perspective essay with no model and no new data. It joins Whittlesea's discrepancy-attribution hypothesis to precision-weighting. The part with moderate support is the reviewed finding that fluency judgements follow discrepancy from expected fluency (the hension effect and its extensions), reported secondhand. The precision reading and the felt/unfelt levels are proposals. "Felt" here means attended and reportable, not phenomenal, and fluency is not offered as affect. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-688](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-688.md) | Options help only with the right subgoals | Botvinick, Niv and Barto (2009), [LIT-581](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-581.md), read in [NOTE-451](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-451.md). Toy simulations in a rooms domain with pre-trained options. Doorway options sped learning; window options slowed it; with a shortcut opened, primitive-only agents found the shortest path on 75% of runs while doorway-option agents never used it (mean 11.79 against 9.73 steps). It is a result about the model. That people or brains work this way is the separate, proposed account [THEORY-484](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-484.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-785](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-785.md) | Meaning depends on what speaker could have said | Frank and Goodman (2012), [LIT-821](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-821.md), and Goodman and Frank's review (2016), [LIT-816](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-816.md), present listener inference as the inversion of an informative speaker, the rational speech act account. The record holds as shown, in [THEORY-172](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-172.md), the fits of that model to mean bets in one-shot reference games and Bergen, Goodman and Levy's signalling-game result. This is the mechanism the fits were offered for, filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 when the narrowing dropped it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-791](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-791.md) | Colour naming lies near the IB bound | Zaslavsky, Kemp, Regier & Tishby (2018), [LIT-810](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-810.md), read in [NOTE-631](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-631.md), using the bound of [LIT-338](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-338.md). Their fit covers the World Color Survey languages and English, with the need distribution over meanings estimated from the same naming data, and that measured part is the Active [THEORY-163](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-163.md). The authors present the result as a property of the world's languages. This THEORY holds that general claim. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-796](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-796.md) | Question-order effects obey the QQ equality | Wang, Solloway, Shiffrin & Busemeyer (2014), [LIT-795](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-795.md), after Wang & Busemeyer (2013), [LIT-834](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-834.md). The general law the PNAS paper proposes, filed apart from what its 66 Pew surveys and 72 studies measured ([THEORY-166](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-166.md)) under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4. The equality is a symmetry of Lüders projectors and a classical model with order events can meet it, so the law does not by itself favour quantum probability. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-800](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-800.md) | Hopfield stores ~0.15N; forgetting keeps recent | The large-N and forgetting clauses that [THEORY-272](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-272.md)'s title carried before the promotion audit (batch 051) narrowed it to Hopfield's simulations at N = 30 and 100.
