Hopfield (1982), [LIT-918](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-918.md), expects the 0.15N figure "for all large N" from a crosstalk estimate, and states in words that overload makes every memory irretrievable unless old ones are forgotten, with saturating couplings as the mechanism. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-807](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-807.md) | Concept combination has a quantum emergent layer | Aerts's reading, which [THEORY-255](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-255.md)'s title carried before the promotion audit narrowed it (batch 018) to the impossibility Theorem 9 proves. Aerts (2009), [LIT-934](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-934.md), read in [NOTE-808](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-808.md), fits the ∆-type deviations with one emergent subspace per pair and reads thought as two superposed layers. The narrowing was right that the theorem does not force an emergent concept, only dropping the meet or the monotone weight; this entry is the emergence reading as Aerts's thesis. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-816](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-816.md) | Size principle follows from informative speakers | Frank, Goodman, Lai and Tenenbaum (2009), [LIT-824](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-824.md), read in [NOTE-627](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-627.md), derive the size principle from an informative speaker and present the word learner as inverting that speaker. The record holds as shown, in [THEORY-472](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-472.md), the derivation and one experiment in which mean bets matched the inversion; in those displays an informative-speaker learner and a plain size-principle learner coincide, so whether learners reason about the speaker is open. [THEORY-785](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-785.md) is the same inversion for listeners in reference games. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-823](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-823.md) | Tetris rotations are epistemic actions | Kirsh and Maglio (1994), [LIT-1054](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1054.md), read in full in [NOTE-878](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-878.md), with Kirsh (1995), [LIT-1076](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1076.md), read in [NOTE-871](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-871.md), argue that the extra, early and checking moves of Tetris players are epistemic actions: physical moves whose primary function is to cut the space, time or unreliability of the player's own computation. The record holds as shown, in [THEORY-360](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-360.md), only the early-rotation timing and the drop-length difference after the wall check. Over-rotation and the rise of the check with drop height rest on figures without printed numbers, and the saving is argued from a three-player pilot, not measured. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 when the narrowing dropped it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-830](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-830.md) | Sustained seeing rests on a stable sensory code | Vishne, Gerber, Knight and Deouell (2023), [LIT-644](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-644.md), read in full in [NOTE-499](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-499.md), conclude from their intracranial recordings that sustained visual experience may rest on a stable sensory representation, with frontoparietal representation serving discrete updates, and propose a stable "experience subspace". Their measurement, in ten patients and for images up to 1.5 s, is the Active [THEORY-102](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-102.md). This is the general claim that measurement was filed to support, held Proposed until a second method or cohort and a case where percept and input come apart test it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-865](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-865.md) v2 | Verbalizable directions carry verbal report | Gurnee, Sofroniew et al. (2026), [LIT-1347](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1347.md), read in [NOTE-1069](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1069.md) (main text in full, appendices in part). It is the functional analogue of conscious access, in the access sense only, found in a transformer and tested by intervention. The sharp edge: one company's models studied by that company, a lens whose own statistics draw the layer band, a flexible/automatic split partly defined by the result, and an explicit refusal to say anything about phenomenal consciousness. | Active |
| [THEORY-869](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-869.md) v2 | Ablating J-space cuts experiential language | Gurnee, Sofroniew et al. (2026), [LIT-1347](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1347.md), §3.5.3 and §A.23, read in [NOTE-1069](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1069.md). The authors conclude that "the J-space supports the model's propensity to provide rich experiential reports, whether about itself or another entity". The sharp edge: the measure is a register of text graded by another model, on five or six prompts per condition, in one company's models; and the effect holds for reports about others, so it is not evidence of anything the self-reports are about. | Active |
| [THEORY-872](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-872.md) | The self is real as a pattern, not a substance | Gładziejewski (2025), [LIT-1360](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1360.md), read in full in [NOTE-1056](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1056.md), §4.1, after Hohwy & Michael (2017) and Letheby & Gerrans (2017), neither of which the record holds. An interpretation, not a result. The paper calls its self section "an initial sketch". It does not say that the self-model exaggerates the self's unity, though the exchange that filed the work said so. It says the single common cause is a compression, and that the verdict on selves turns on criteria. Its one candidate for a self-model that misdescribes is a dissociative case better compressed by two narrative selves. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-873](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-873.md) v2 | Consciousness claims caricature attention | Graziano (2024), [LIT-1358](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1358.md), read in full in [NOTE-1071](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1071.md): the attention schema theory and its "deep illusionism", in an essay with no new data. Arrow B is an argument. The identification of the target with attention rests on covariation with report cited from others, and the merging of attention, workspace and integration is asserted. Its "small" illusionism keeps the modelled process real and denies the reported phenomenal essence, so it is the strong illusionism of [THEORY-633](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-633.md) with a named target, not the weak kind. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-874](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-874.md) | Organicism is orthogonal to embodiment | Ward (2026), [LIT-1356](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1356.md), read in the accepted manuscript in [NOTE-1065](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1065.md). Views differ on where cognition's processes are (skull or brain–body–world) and, separately, on what the meaning of mental states depends on (information, or organization distinctive of the living). Embodied predictive processing, extended functionalism and cybernetics are embodied and informationalist; the enactive approach is organicist, and further marked by experiential primacy and reciprocity. The sharp edge: it is a taxonomy argued from examples and exegesis. It does not argue that organicism is true, and the line between distinctive and characteristic properties of life is left without a criterion. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-877](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-877.md) | Manifest image is structural; envatted alike | Gładziejewski (2025), [LIT-1360](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1360.md), read in full in [NOTE-1056](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1056.md), §§2–3, drawing on Chalmers's structuralism and veridicalism (2018, 2022), which the record does not hold. The cognitive half rests on a realist reading of predictive processing and on an analogy between free energy and description length. The veridicalism follows only if manifest content is wholly structural, which is assumed. Projective properties (cuteness) are allowed at one end of a continuum. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-878](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-878.md) | Reappraisal partly runs apart from generation | Bo et al. (preprint 2023, published 2024), [LIT-1359](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1359.md), read in full from the bioRxiv v2 preprint in [NOTE-1061](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1061.md). Two fMRI samples (n = 182 and 176), voxelwise Bayes factors, every effect replicated in both. Sixteen regions are engaged by reappraisal and show 10:1 evidence of no response to negative against neutral pictures without it; fourteen, the larger set, are engaged by both. The selective set best predicts how much reported negative affect falls. One instructed strategy, one stimulus type, BOLD only; nothing shows the selective regions do the regulating. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-879](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-879.md) | Sensory quality alone doesn't make experience | Lycan (2000; rev. 2023), [LIT-1355](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1355.md), read in full in [NOTE-1068](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1068.md). The entry defends the distinction in its own voice (§4.2, §5.1), crediting Carruthers (2000) for the distinction and Armstrong, Nelkin, Rosenthal and Lycan for the claim that qualities can go unnoticed. It is argued, not shown. Its one case, the driver "on autopilot", is the case Block reads the other way, and the entry gives no evidence that the driver's perception was not experienced and forgotten. It concerns the quality experienced, not emotion or affect, and it does not say what awareness is. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-886](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-886.md) | Prediction error spikes mark event boundaries | Zacks, Speer, Swallow, Braver & Reynolds (2007), [LIT-1382](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1382.md), read in full in [NOTE-1084](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1084.md) from the PMC author manuscript. Event segmentation theory: a theory and review, with a partial network simulation and mostly correlational evidence. Prediction error is never measured in people, and the one neural prediction checked (anterior cingulate responses at boundaries) failed. It is a theory of a passive observer of others' activity; it does not cover one's own intentions, and does not mention the doorway effect. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-888](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-888.md) | Doorways impair memory via event interference | From the Radvansky lab's doorway studies, [LIT-1392](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1392.md), [LIT-1384](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1384.md) and [LIT-1385](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1385.md), read in full in [NOTE-1083](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1083.md), [NOTE-1082](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1082.md) and [NOTE-1081](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1081.md), and the independent conceptual replication of McFadyen et al., [LIT-1387](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1387.md), read in [NOTE-1079](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1079.md). The pattern (a cost on the carried object, worse after two new rooms, not helped by returning) replicates within the lab's paradigm; the interference account is reached by eliminating alternatives, and the independent study found no loss of hits, only more false alarms under load. It is about recognizing object labels, not intentions. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-900](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-900.md) v2 | Avoidance evidence favours expectancy accounts | Mancinelli & Bach (preprint 2025; NBR 2026), [LIT-1477](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1477.md), read in full in [NOTE-1134](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1134.md). A PRISMA review without meta-analysis, searched to December 2024, of studies with shock or noise in healthy volunteers. The verdict is the authors' scoring of five theories against phenomena they rate for robustness; no model was fitted. They argue current paradigms are too simple to expose where inference gives way to Pavlovian control. | Active |
| [THEORY-908](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-908.md) v2 | If-then plans outperform mere scheduling | Sheeran, Listrom & Gollwitzer (2024), [LIT-1488](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1488.md), read in full in [NOTE-1131](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1131.md). Table 3's moderators across 642 tests: contingent format .43 (k = 373), schedule .29 (k = 269); rehearsal .45 against .33; recording .31 against .44; visualising the response no effect. The authors read the recording and elaboration costs as deliberation undermining automaticity. Between-test and uncorrected for bias. | Active |
| [THEORY-913](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-913.md) v2 | If-then plans hand response control to the cue | Gollwitzer & Sheeran (2006), [LIT-1497](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1497.md), read in full in [NOTE-1124](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1124.md). The component-process tables of the 94-test meta-analysis: large effects for the accessibility of the planned cue and for the immediacy, efficiency and non-conscious running of the planned response, each from one to seven tests, fixed-effect, without a bias correction. Only cue accessibility and cue–response link strength had been tested as mediators. The authors' gloss is "instant habits". | Active |
| [THEORY-959](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-959.md) | Constancies are invariants within experience | Isaac (2025), [LIT-1361](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1361.md), read in [NOTE-1163](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1163.md): the group-theoretic layer of a structuralist account of experience. The paper's evidence supports the weaker half: constancy needs invariance under transformations internal to experience. The stronger half, that this invariance is what makes experience objective and induces a subject–object distinction, is Cassirer's, argued from the co-presence of two levels of experience, and the paper gives no way to tell invariant extraction with a subject from invariant extraction without one. "Group-theoretic" is used loosely: the paper's own examples are groupoids or toy models. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-982](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-982.md) | Claude 3.5 Haiku plans ahead within a pass | Lindsey et al. (2025), [LIT-1541](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1541.md), read in [NOTE-1181](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1181.md): the introduction ("Claude 3.5 Haiku routinely uses multiple intermediate reasoning steps 'in its head'"; "It displays signs of forward planning") and the discussion's sections on plan formation and working backward from a goal. The case studies show each mechanism on chosen prompts, and the same article has a case without it: on a jailbreak the model "doesn't know what it plans to say until it actually says it". The authors report a satisfying graph for about a quarter of the prompts they try. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-984](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-984.md) | Haiku composes Dallas→Texas→Austin in two hops | Lindsey et al. (2025), [LIT-1541](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1541.md), read in [NOTE-1181](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1181.md). A two-hop intermediate, measured by intervention on one prompt. The evidence that counts is the change of output under the swaps; the graph itself is of the replacement model. It does not say how often the model reasons in two steps, nor that the shortcut path is weak. | Active |
| [THEORY-1017](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1017.md) | Haiku plans rhymes before writing the line | Lindsey et al. (2025), [LIT-1541](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1541.md), read in [NOTE-1181](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1181.md). A target word represented before the text that leads to it, and used causally: it is the case study's own measurement, on one couplet and a 25-poem injection test. It does not say how widespread planning is, the "about half" being a count without a stated sample, and one of the article's displayed "success cases" does not end in the injected word. | Active |
| [THEORY-1018](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1018.md) | Acrostic jailbreak isn't recognized until written | Lindsey et al. (2025), [LIT-1541](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1541.md), read in [NOTE-1181](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1181.md). On this prompt the model "doesn't know what it plans to say until it actually says it". It is one prompt, partly effective, and the decisive refusal mechanism runs through attention, which the graphs do not show: the injection that produced a refusal needed attention left unfrozen. | Active |
| [THEORY-1072](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1072.md) | Well-structuredness is solver-relative and graded | Simon (1973), [LIT-1634](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1634.md), read in [NOTE-1232](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1232.md) from a scan of the published article. Active as a conceptual argument the paper makes in full: six conditions for a well structured problem, read with condition 6 as practicable computation, worked through for theorem proving and chess. It does not say that structuring is the whole of problem solving, which Simon rejects, or that any problem is ill structured for every solver. | Active |
| [THEORY-1084](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1084.md) v3 | Ill-structured problems need no new mechanism | Simon (1973), [LIT-1634](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1634.md), read in [NOTE-1232](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1232.md). The alternation is described for an architect, matched to a 1923 account of battleship design by an organization and to the NSS chess program, and argued from the seriality of the solver; nothing is implemented or tested, and Simon states the last part as what his analysis "suggests" and as "reason to be optimistic". Active as a report of the proposal; whether it is right, which wants a test, is THEORY-1216, Proposed. | Active |
| [THEORY-1110](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1110.md) | dACC specifies control by its expected value | What the expected-value-of-control paper proposes, split from [THEORY-070](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-070.md) by the sixth status review ([ADR-058](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-058.md)'s route) so that a claim needing only the proposal can stand on it. The paper was read in full ([NOTE-446](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-446.md)), so the reading of what it proposes is held. Whether the proposal is true, a fit of the computation and a dissociation of specifying from implementing, stays [THEORY-070](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-070.md)'s question, Proposed. | Active |
| [THEORY-1112](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1112.md) | Groupness needs inferred collective intention | Skorich (2025, v2 2026), [LIT-1765](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1765.md), a preprint. Categorization with accentuation makes members interchangeable, not one, since a category is a set and a set is internally differentiated. Groups such as orchestras and families need no similarity. Groups are holistic entities perceived from cues to shared mental states, much as faces are perceived from configuration. Reported support: four experiments under review in which groups defined by a mental state (a chosen T-shirt colour; seeing the duck or the rabbit) drew more favouritism and tracking than groups defined by a physical property. Proposed: the argument is conceptual and the evidence is unpublished. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1124](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1124.md) | Log co-occurrences act as Euclidean distances | Hashimoto, Alvarez-Melis and Jaakkola (2016), [LIT-1801](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1801.md), §3, read in [NOTE-1329](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1329.md). The correlation follows a normalization chosen to maximize it; the two nearest-neighbour statistics are necessary conditions, the corpora exceed the asymptotic centrality bound and pass only a non-asymptotic range, and the free-association data fail the reciprocity criterion the paper states. Proposed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1154](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1154.md) | Analogies map related systems, not attributes | Gentner (1983), [LIT-1810](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1810.md), read in [NOTE-1349](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1349.md). Argued from worked examples (the Rutherford analogy, heat and water) with one study, summarized without statistics, showing relational content dominating interpretations of analogies but not descriptions of objects. The systematicity principle is stated as a likelihood on p. 163 and as determination in the abstract and summary. The rules work on a predicate structure the theory takes as given, which its footnote 4 concedes is a modelling choice. Proposed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1175](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1175.md) | If-then plans beat when-where scheduling | The wide form [THEORY-908](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-908.md) held before the tenth status review narrowed it, kept as a Proposed reading by the [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind-1 sweep of 2026-10-30: the source asserts it, and [THEORY-908](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-908.md), Active, is its evidence. Sheeran, Listrom & Gollwitzer (2024), [LIT-1488](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1488.md), conclude that the if-then format leads to superior impact, that rehearsal helps and that revisiting a kept copy makes plans less effective; their evidence is between-test moderator contrasts, uncorrected for bias. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1194](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1194.md) v2 | Coupled external stores can carry beliefs | What the extended-mind paper argues, split from [THEORY-579](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-579.md) by the sixteenth status review on [THEORY-1110](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1110.md)'s pattern ([ADR-058](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-058.md)'s route), so that [CLAIM-175](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-175.md), which argues "on the extended-mind thesis's own terms", can stand on the statement of those terms. Both papers were read in full ([NOTE-180](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-180.md), [NOTE-363](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-363.md)), and Clark (2005) says in his own words that the parity principle was not argued. Whether the conditional holds, that coupling of this kind makes a store part of a mind, stays [THEORY-579](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-579.md)'s question, Proposed. | Active |
| [THEORY-1196](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1196.md) | Typeless neurons still separate nearly all splits | The wide form of Posani et al. (2026), [LIT-708](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-708.md), kept here when the status review of 2026-10-30 narrowed [THEORY-124](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-124.md) to what their analysis of the IBL Brainwide Map measured and promoted it ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md); [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md), kind 1). The paper asserts that cortical representations are rarely categorical and highly separable. One task, overtrained mice, eight variables and a lenient separability criterion. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1216](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1216.md) | Ill-structured problems need no new mechanisms | The thesis Simon (1973), [LIT-1634](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1634.md), proposes, kept here when the twenty-second status review promoted [THEORY-1084](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1084.md) as a report of the proposal ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md); [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md), kind 1). The paper describes the architecture, matches it to an architect, to battleship design and to a chess program, and argues from the seriality of the solver; nothing is built or tested, and Simon states the last part as what his analysis "suggests". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1224](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1224.md) | Ablating J-space mutes experiential register | The wide form of Gurnee, Sofroniew et al. (2026), [LIT-1347](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1347.md), section 3.5.3, kept here when the status review of 2026-10-30 narrowed [THEORY-869](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-869.md) to what the ablation measured and promoted it ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md); [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md), kind 1). The authors conclude that "the J-space supports the model's propensity to provide rich experiential reports, whether about itself or another entity" (p. 28). The measure is a model-graded register on few prompts, in one company's models, with no register control and no blind human rating. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1226](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1226.md) | A sparse J-space is privileged for verbal report | The wide form of Gurnee, Sofroniew et al. (2026), [LIT-1347](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1347.md), kept here when the status review of 2026-10-30 narrowed [THEORY-865](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-865.md) to what their experiments measured and promoted it ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md); [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md), kind 1). The paper asserts that verbalizable representations form a global workspace in language models. Its tests are on four models of one family, by their makers, with a selectivity split partly defined by the result; no independent replication is reported. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1239](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1239.md) | Logistic systems can't carry commonsense defaults | Minsky's (1974) further claim against logic, from the frames memo's appendix ([LIT-410](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-410.md), read in [NOTE-337](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-337.md), C7). It was kept here when the twenty-fourth status review promoted [THEORY-462](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-462.md) ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md) §3; [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md), kind 1). Monotonicity is a correct observation about classical logic. The memo asserts that no repair can succeed: "I think such attempts will continue to fail". The record holds no reading of the non-monotonic logics that were built to repair it. The condition is carried over word for word, so "the account" in it now means this entry, and "its first half" means [THEORY-462](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-462.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1240](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1240.md) | Chat models follow narrative, not fixed truth | The wider thesis Bottou and Schölkopf assume, filed beside [THEORY-547](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-547.md) by the twenty-fourth status review ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md) §3; [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 1). [THEORY-547](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-547.md), Active, holds what follows from their idealization; whether deployed chat models share that nature is this entry's question, and its promote_when is [THEORY-547](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-547.md)'s old condition, word for word. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1242](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1242.md) | Early vision tracks retinal info, losses central | The thesis Geisler's review asserts, filed beside [THEORY-336](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-336.md) by the status review of 2026-10-30 ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md) §3; [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 1). [THEORY-336](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-336.md), Active, holds what the review reports; whether the parallel holds is this entry's question, and none of the primary stage-by-stage studies (Geisler 1989; Banks, Geisler and Bennett 1987) is read. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1290](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1290.md) v2 | Fit alone can't choose among dynamical models | Bechtel and Abrahamsen (2010), [LIT-1936](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1936.md), read in [NOTE-1492](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1492.md). Circadian models came after the clock's parts were found in the laboratory, and they explore those parts' dynamics. Cognitive models posit their parts. "Empirical evidence can rule out specific models, but usually cannot decide between competing architectures" (p. 332). It does not say de novo models are worthless: they make the same six kinds of contribution, at weaker standing. Nor does it say that anchoring makes a model right. | Active |
| [THEORY-1296](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1296.md) v2 | Deliberation selects from mind-wandering's stream | Metzinger (2017), [LIT-1945](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1945.md), pp. 11–17, read in [NOTE-1496](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1496.md). The "cognitive affordance hypothesis": mind-wandering is "mental sleep-walking" that "sets up the inner world" of candidate mental actions, and frontal control "latch[es] onto the best candidate". Offered as a hypothesis after Clark and Cisek's affordance competition, with no data. The second clause is the chapter's own statement that the data "do not help to decide" what the epistemic agent model does, which takes back the principle the 2015 paper stated. "Best" is not defined, so the hypothesis does not say whether selection is by the candidates' content or by relations that govern them. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1297](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1297.md) v2 | Mind-wandering takes half, not two-thirds, of time | Metzinger (2013), [LIT-1942](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1942.md), restated in 2015, [LIT-1941](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1941.md); read in [NOTE-1495](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1495.md) and [NOTE-1497](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1497.md). The identification is conceptual: an episode of unintentional mind-wandering cannot, while it runs, be suspended or ended at will, and veto is what M-autonomy turns on. The share is computed from others' figures, and recomputed here: 631 of 1207 conscious minutes, 52%, against the "roughly two thirds" both papers state. Proposed: no measure of veto during episodes is reported, and the 30–50% figures count task-unrelated thought, which includes deliberate daydreaming the definition excludes. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1298](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1298.md) v2 | Self-model claims control's return as one's act | Metzinger (2015), [LIT-1941](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1941.md), pp. 289–292, read in [NOTE-1497](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1497.md); first in 2013 ([LIT-1942](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1942.md), pp. 4, 11) and widened in 2017 ([LIT-1945](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1945.md), pp. 20–21) to the sense of origination in agency generally. It rests on Schooler et al. (2011) and Wegner (2002), neither read, and on the argument that a self-model which must represent itself as always having had the ability cannot represent its return as caused from outside. A hypothesis: no episode is reported in which the cause of a return and the report of it were recorded apart. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1300](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1300.md) | Mind-wandering hides veto, doesn't remove it | Metzinger (2015), [LIT-1941](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1941.md), pp. 280–283 and 296, read in [NOTE-1497](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1497.md); anticipated in 2013 ([LIT-1942](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1942.md), p. 3, note 4). The "moderate, nuanced position": what is lost is "not the ability itself" but "conscious knowledge of our potential for second-order mental action", with the "principle of 'Autonomy by Phenomenal Self-Representation'". Both are stated, not argued, and neither is tested. Metzinger's 2017 chapter ([LIT-1945](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1945.md), pp. 13–14) says the data cannot decide whether the self-model constitutes, enables or only accompanies control, which withholds the principle's causal reading. "Deliberately" also does work: inhibition can be wholly subpersonal. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1317](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1317.md) | High gamma coupling to 2–5 Hz tracks attention | Szczepanski et al. (2014), [LIT-1982](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1982.md), read in [NOTE-1528](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1528.md) from the publisher's open-access PDF. Active for what it states: the reported counts (123 of 273 electrodes coupled; 55 stronger contralaterally; 28 correlating with RT, r(41) = −0.51 and r(47) = −0.37 in the examples) were checked against the text, and the ERP and power controls are in it. The sharp edge is the causal one: no manipulation of the coupling was made, and the paper's "facilitate" and Jennings's "improve" outrun it. | Active |
| [THEORY-1354](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1354.md) | People learn abstract causal functional forms | Lucas & Griffiths (2010), [LIT-2018](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2018.md), read in full in [NOTE-1543](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1543.md). Five blicket-meter experiments: training that suggests a conjunctive, noisy-disjunctive or deterministic form changes judgments of new objects in an identical test block, and more within a domain than across; a two-parameter sigmoid model fits the mean ratings (r = 0.98–0.99). Proposed: small samples, in-sample fits against rivals that cannot vary between conditions, one reversed prediction, one marginal effect, and no preregistered replication read. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1356](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1356.md) | People build latent task-sets unprompted | Collins and Frank (2013), [LIT-2012](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2012.md), read in [NOTE-1545](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1545.md). Proposed: positive transfer replicated across the paper's two experiments (N = 33, N = 35) but is modest (t = 2.37, p = .024 in Experiment 1), and the negative-transfer interaction was significant over the whole group only in Experiment 1, a trend in Experiment 2. The EEG follow-up re-analyses Experiment 2's participants, so it is no independent replication. The account is behavioural; it does not say people perform Bayesian inference over task-sets, which the authors disclaim, nor that the Chinese-restaurant reuse prior is what people use, which they leave untested. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1357](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1357.md) v3 | Stroke programs match humans at one-shot letters | Lake, Salakhutdinov & Tenenbaum (2015), [LIT-2009](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2009.md), main text and Supplementary Materials read in [NOTE-1542](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1542.md). BPL erred 3.3% against people's 4.5% on 20-way one-shot classification within 10 held-out Omniglot alphabets; judges identified its productions at 49–59% in four visual Turing tests; lesions without token-level learning to learn or without compositionality erred 11.0% and 14.0% and were easier to detect, while removing the type-level priors left classification at 3.5%. Active as the reported measurements, read with the Supplementary Materials' lesions and controls. Independent replication is QUESTION-446's. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Active |
| [THEORY-1358](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1358.md) | Causal schemas enable one-shot causal learning | Kemp, Goodman & Tenenbaum (2010), [LIT-2008](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2008.md), read in [NOTE-1551](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1551.md). A causal schema, a CRP partition of objects with category-level causal models, features and pairwise interactions, sits above object-level causal Bayes nets; four adult experiments in one paradigm show one-shot and zero-shot causal learning and overruling, matched qualitatively better than two baselines, with two misfits. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1359](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1359.md) | Interventions also seek causal overhypotheses | Jiang & Lucas (2024), [LIT-2014](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2014.md), read in [NOTE-1546](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1546.md) (appendices not read). Two preregistered online blicket experiments. Learners that ignore form information or hold one fixed form barely beat random at predicting interventions; the model that does not transfer edges the full model on average (.059 against .055), while per participant the full model is best for the largest group, whose fitted weights mostly favour form information. Proposed: the transfer clause is the weakest, failing at the group level. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1360](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1360.md) | Observers infer whether cues share a cause | Körding et al. (2007), [LIT-2010](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2010.md), read in full in [NOTE-1541](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1541.md). Proposed: one experiment of the authors' own (19 subjects) and a refit of Wallace et al.'s (2004) published data support it, against forced fusion, segregation, a MAP rule and two interaction priors, but the rule that commits to the more probable structure was not compared and only a split-half check tests held-out prediction. It does not say how the prior over causal structure is learned, that the inference is automatic, or that the model is hierarchical; that word is A's, from the owner's pasted synthesis. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1361](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1361.md) | Mind reading is inverting a rational planner | Baker, Jara-Ettinger, Saxe and Tenenbaum (2017), [LIT-2013](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2013.md), read in full in [NOTE-1549](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1549.md). Proposed: two experiments (16 and 176 adults) support it against the lesioned models, but the motion heuristic tied on Experiment 1 beliefs, the desire fit carries no information within scenario type, and the test is cross-validation over the authors' own scenarios. It is a computational-level claim, not an account of the algorithm; it does not say the model is hierarchical, a word that is A's, from the owner's pasted synthesis. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1363](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1363.md) | Shape bias is a learned hyperparameter | Kemp, Perfors & Tenenbaum (2007), [LIT-2017](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2017.md), read in [NOTE-1544](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1544.md). Learning a constraint is inference over a hierarchy's higher-level parameters (α, β): low within-category variability of shape is the shape bias. The model reproduces Smith et al.'s first- and second-order generalization qualitatively, with no new experiments, and misses the no-name condition. Computational level; the structure and top prior are given. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1364](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1364.md) | Task-set structure shows in prefrontal EEG | Collins, Cavanagh and Frank (2014), [LIT-2007](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2007.md), read in [NOTE-1550](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1550.md). Proposed: one sample, the participants of Collins and Frank's (2013) Experiment 2 (N = 35; 33 for ERP, 32 for classification), with several uncorrected topographic tests and an early-positivity window chosen from the grand average. The late switch negativity tracked the context dimension but did not predict transfer; the early positivity, absent at group level, and the decoder did (ρ = 0.5, ρ = 0.35), and agreed with each other only marginally. The context dimension is assigned from behavioural switch-costs, so the EEG does not read out the structure independently. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1458](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1458.md) v2 | Scarcity focus leads to costly borrowing | Shah, Shafir & Mullainathan, working paper (before 2012), [LIT-2171](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2171.md), read in [NOTE-1653](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1653.md): an earlier version of their Science paper, standing in for its Experiments 3 and 4. Three borrowing experiments, two with time (n = 143, 118) and one with guesses (n = 76), and one test of the mechanism (n = 33). Active as a report; its limits: the samples are small, and only the authors have replicated the borrowing result, for time and for shots, not for guesses; the focus-to-neglect link weakened in their replications. | Active |
| [THEORY-1484](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1484.md) v3 | Scarcity borrowing replicates, but smaller | Shah, Mullainathan & Shafir (2018), [LIT-2157](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2157.md), read in [NOTE-1686](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1686.md): the authors' write-up of their direct replications, which stands in for the original analyses of the unread Science paper. The sharp edges: the replications are the authors' own, on one online pool, and no team other than the authors has replicated the borrowing or focus studies; the only independent replication, of Study 1, failed as theirs did. | Active |
| [THEORY-1519](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1519.md) v2 | Generative AI polarizes task complexity | Simkute, Tankelevitch et al. (2024), [LIT-2223](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2223.md), read in full in NOTE-1711. A synthesis: the polarization is Human Factors research's finding for automation (credited to Lee and Seppelt, among others), and the generative-AI evidence is a set of user studies, mostly in programming; the paper runs no study. Read as a stand-in for Bainbridge (1983), [LIT-2225](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2225.md), which it cites for the general irony, not for this. It says nothing about the skill the user loses on the easy share. | Active |
| [THEORY-1520](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1520.md) v3 | Tutoring favours more help, not less | Koedinger and Aleven (2007), [LIT-2226](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2226.md), read in full in [NOTE-1708](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1708.md). Held as a report of what the source holds, its truth left to THEORY-1547; the caveats: a narrative review by the Cognitive Tutors' developers, whose component results mostly come without effect sizes, and whose fading result rests on one conference paper. It says that "within a context of tutored problem solving, information should be withheld very sparingly" (p. 255), not that help should be given in general, and it gives no tested switch point. It bears on [CLAIM-602](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-602.md) and [CLAIM-600](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-600.md) as the case of capacity-first support in a learner. | Active |
| [THEORY-1521](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1521.md) v4 | Automated subtasks' skills decay unnoticed | Macnamara et al. (2024), [LIT-2224](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2224.md), read in full in [NOTE-1710](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1710.md). A theoretical perspective with no data of its own. The decay with disuse, and its being larger for cognitive tasks, are the cited literature's (Arthur et al.; Ackerman and Tatel); the selective loss in pilots is Casner et al. (2014), reported second-hand, without sample or sizes; the concealment is the authors' argument, not a finding. Read as a stand-in for Bainbridge (1983), [LIT-2225](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2225.md), on the skill-decay irony only; the paper does not cite her. It does not give a rate, a recovery time, or any test of its extension to AI assistants. | Active |
| [THEORY-1522](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1522.md) v4 | Train skills before AI, inject AI failures | Ahn (2025), [LIT-2222](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2222.md), read in full in [NOTE-1713](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1713.md). The remedies are his proposals for medical curricula, untested. A single-author commentary with no data. | Active |

| [THEORY-2234](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2234.md) | Sign content comes from producer–consumer history | Millikan (2009), "Biosemantics", [LIT-3103](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3103.md), read in [NOTE-2324](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2324.md) from her pre-print. Her own short statement of the selection-based teleosemantics the record said it owed ([LEAD-018](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-018.md)). Teleology explains how a representation can be false; a mapping theory with producer and consumer explains what it represents. Corroborates [CLAIM-650](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-650.md) on its question (a), with a qualification argued in [ARG-204](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-204.md); grounds the objection [CLAIM-920](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-920.md) to [CLAIM-648](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-648.md). Proposed: one reading, of a compressed statement whose account of function is cited, not given. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2235](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2235.md) | Teleosemantics derives content from function | Neander and Schulte (2004; rev. 2022), SEP, "Teleological Theories of Mental Content", [LIT-3104](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3104.md), read in [NOTE-2325](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2325.md). A survey by two proponents, one of whom is surveyed. It reports the field's shape and its objections and settles little; the title asserts only what the survey reports. Read for [LEAD-018](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-018.md) beside Millikan's own statement ([THEORY-2234](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2234.md)). Proposed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2239](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2239.md) | Bilinguals split green-blue without borrowing | Malik-Moraleda, Mahowald, Conway and Gibson (2023), [LIT-3108](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3108.md), read in [NOTE-2330](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2330.md) (supplement unread). Against 71 monolinguals, 30 bilinguals' Tsimane' colour terms have lower average surprisal (4.42 against 5.16), cover fewer chips, and overlap less with their neighbours; shandyes and yụshñus, one green-blue category for monolinguals (KL 0.10), separate (1.18). No Spanish term is borrowed. Between-group and colour only; the bilinguals also live in a more industrialised town. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2241](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2241.md) | Brief mindfulness speeds responses briefly | Ge et al. (2024), [LIT-916](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-916.md), read in [NOTE-2331](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2331.md) for [LEAD-078](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-078.md). In 70 students low in trait mindfulness, monitor-and-acceptance training sped conflict and inhibition responses at post-test, left accuracy and delay discounting unchanged, and had no effect at follow-up. A dissociation of speed from discounting, not a test of whether discounting mediates a change in self-control: [ARG-206](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-206.md) holds that it does not show [CLAIM-156](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-156.md)'s route. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2264](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2264.md) | Frontal tDCS raises mind-wandering | Axelrod, Rees, Lavidor and Bar (2015), [LIT-3135](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3135.md), read in [NOTE-2357](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2357.md). Two small experiments (n = 14 and 31). The causal clause is the authors' inference; the executive-capacity clause rests on a non-significant rise in target detection. The effect was replicated by the first author ([THEORY-2265](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2265.md)) and not in a pre-registered three-lab study ([THEORY-2266](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2266.md)), so the two accounts rival. It does not say that the stimulation changed the agent's awareness of its own thought or control, which was not measured, and so it is not a test of Metzinger's H1, which the 2017 chapter ([LIT-1945](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1945.md), p. 14) cited it for. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2265](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2265.md) | tDCS mind-wandering effect bypasses meta-awareness | Axelrod, Zhu and Qiu (2018), [LIT-3134](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3134.md), read in [NOTE-2355](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2355.md): a direct replication of [THEORY-2264](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2264.md)'s experiment (n = 85) with a meta-awareness probe added. The second clause is the authors' inference, that "at least in some cases mind-wandering might not be regulated by meta-awareness". It rivals the pre-registered null of [THEORY-2266](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2266.md). For the record it is the nearest the literature comes to Metzinger's H1, and it is not a test of it: the rated awareness is of attention's location, not of the capacity to end a thought, and it was not manipulated. It bears on [QUESTION-367](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-367.md) only as weak evidence that the rate of mind-wandering can move while the agent's self-rating does not. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2266](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2266.md) | Frontal tDCS fails to raise mind-wandering | Boayue and ten colleagues (2019/2020), [LIT-3133](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3133.md), read from the authors' preprint in [NOTE-2358](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2358.md): a pre-registered three-lab replication (n = 192) of [THEORY-2264](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2264.md)'s experiment, with d = -0.11 (HDI [-0.38, 0.17]), BF 10.65 for the null against a positive effect, and a replication Bayes factor of 0.002. The false-positive clause is the authors' inference. It rivals [THEORY-2264](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2264.md) and the first author's positive replication, [THEORY-2265](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2265.md), which it predates and does not discuss. Whether it corrects [THEORY-2264](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2264.md) is left to the owner. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2277](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2277.md) | PTSD delays first gaze to background context | Zidda, Steiger-White, Winkelmann, Ruttorf, Andoh, Nees & Flor (2025), [LIT-3174](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3174.md), read in full in [NOTE-2406](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2406.md). A gaze bias against the context of a trauma cue, specific to PTSD against trauma-exposed controls, measured only as the latency of the first look, and tied to poorer relational memory. The nearest study found to the first half of [QUESTION-303](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-303.md); it has no recall manipulation, and its background does not disambiguate. Proposed until replicated. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2284](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2284.md) | PTSD gaze lingers on trauma; rest is thin | Diotaiuti, Spica, Di Siena, Cavicchiolo, De Souza, Andrade & Mancone (2026), [LIT-3179](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3179.md), read in full in [NOTE-2382](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2382.md). A map of what the eye-tracking literature on PTSD has measured. For [QUESTION-303](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-303.md) it is a check on absence: no included study measures gaze after cued recall, and the use of gaze to track engagement with corrective context in exposure is called hypothetical. The last clause of the title is the reader's count from the review's Table 1, not a sentence of the review. The corpus misses at least two eligible studies. Proposed until an independent search agrees. | Proposed |
